title: The Penny Blue
subject: A woman goes to the Saturday stamp fair in a church hall to buy one gift, keeps returning to the same dealer's table asking for the penny blue, and is really watching his careful tweezers.
caption: Cool-jazz waltz in 3/4, West Coast vocal jazz trio-plus-horn sound. Brushed snare in a slow waltz pattern, upright bass walking in three, muted flugelhorn answering the vocal phrases, nylon-string guitar comping soft seventh chords, sparse piano fills. Intimate small-room jazz-club mix, natural room ambience, warm analogue tone. Female alto, warm and steady, gentle phrasing with clear diction. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 96 BPM, F major. Tender, warm, unhurried. No rap, no autotune, no drum machine, no distorted guitar, no synthesizer, no swing-big-band brass section.
lyrics:
[Intro - brushes, upright bass, muted flugelhorn]

[Verse 1]
Saturday in the church hall
Trestle tables, folding chairs
I came to buy one stamp, that's all
A gift for my brother, nothing more

[Pre-Chorus]
You lift it with your tweezers
Like it might say something back

[Chorus]
Show me the penny blue again
Slowly, slowly, hold it in the light
I don't need the penny blue
I just need to watch your hands

[Verse 2]
Third week now I'm at your table
You know my name, I know your glass
You measure every little tooth
I count the hours till next Saturday

[Pre-Chorus]
You lift it with your tweezers
Like it might say something back

[Chorus]
Show me the penny blue once more
Pretend there's a flaw along the edge
I don't need the penny blue
I just need to watch your hands

[Bridge - guitar and bass only]
Seventeen pounds, I leave a twenty

[Chorus]
Keep the penny blue, my love
Keep it safe inside the album
All I wanted was the Saturday
And the way you hold a small thing

[Outro - flugelhorn, brushes fade]
Show me the penny blue
